ProbableCauses: Worn spark plugs or ignition coils; clogged fuel injector; vacuum leak; low compression in a cylinder

ProbableCauses: Low coolant; failed thermostat; radiator blockage; failed water pump or cooling fan

ProbableCauses: Age/mileage past replacement interval; oil contamination; failed tensioner

ProbableCauses: Ageing catalyst; repeated misfires melting the substrate; oil/coolant contamination

RecommendedAction: Confirm with an emissions/backpressure test; replace if clogged

ProbableCauses: Sensor ageing; carbon fouling; wiring damage

RecommendedAction: Replace the faulty sensor; typically restores fuel economy

ProbableCauses: Worn pump motor; clogged strainer; running tank near-empty habitually; relay/wiring fault

RecommendedAction: Test fuel pressure; replace pump/strainer as needed

ProbableCauses: Fuel deposits; poor fuel quality; failing injector solenoid

RecommendedAction: Get injectors cleaned or serviced ultrasonically

ProbableCauses: Corroded pipe/silencer; failed gasket; cracked manifold

RecommendedAction: Repair promptly; carbon monoxide ingress is a health hazard

ProbableCauses: Low/burnt ATF; worn clutch packs; failing torque converter; solenoid fault
PrecautionarySteps: Avoid overtaking and hills; check ATF level and colour
RecommendedAction: Transmission specialist inspection needed; delay increases repair cost sharply
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Low fluid; degraded fluid; solenoid/valve-body wear; TCM adaptation issues

RecommendedAction: Fluid change and solenoid diagnostics recommended
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Friction disc worn; oil-contaminated disc; failing pressure plate; riding the clutch
PrecautionarySteps: Avoid holding the car on hills with the clutch; carry momentum where safe
RecommendedAction: Replace the clutch kit; slipping accelerates rapidly once started
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Failed pan gasket; axle seal leak; loose drain plug; damaged cooler line
PrecautionarySteps: Check fluid before driving; do not drive if shifting deteriorates
RecommendedAction: Repair the leak and refill with the correct fluid spec
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Degraded CVT fluid; worn belt/pulleys; software calibration
PrecautionarySteps: Use gentle throttle from standstill; verify correct CVT fluid used at last service
RecommendedAction: CVT fluid replacement and TCM update at an authorised workshop
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Pads worn to wear indicator; glazed pads; seized caliper causing uneven wear
PrecautionarySteps: Increase following distance; brake gently and early; avoid heavy loads
RecommendedAction: Replace pads (and check discs) immediately; grinding means metal-on-metal damage
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Heat distortion from hard braking; uneven pad deposits; over-torqued wheel nuts
PrecautionarySteps: Avoid high-speed hard braking; increase following distance
RecommendedAction: Machine or replace rotors and fit new pads
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Corroded brake line; failed caliper/wheel-cylinder seal; loose fitting; failing master cylinder
PrecautionarySteps: Do not drive — a soft pedal can become no pedal; check reservoir level
RecommendedAction: Tow to workshop; repair leak, replace fluid, bleed the system
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Wheel-speed sensor failure; damaged tone ring; ABS module/pump fault; wiring
PrecautionarySteps: Brakes still work but without anti-lock — brake earlier and avoid hard braking on wet roads
RecommendedAction: Scan ABS codes and replace the faulty sensor/module
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Battery aged 3-5 yrs; parasitic drain; short trips never fully charging; extreme heat damage
PrecautionarySteps: Carry jumper cables or a jump pack; switch off accessories before starting
RecommendedAction: Load-test the battery and charging system; replace if weak

ProbableCauses: Worn brushes/regulator; failed diode; loose/worn drive belt
PrecautionarySteps: Switch off non-essential electricals; expect the car to die once the battery drains — avoid highways
RecommendedAction: Test charging voltage (should be ~13.8-14.4V); replace alternator or belt
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Worn solenoid contacts; failing motor; flywheel ring-gear damage; loose earth strap
PrecautionarySteps: Park where a jump/push start or assistance is possible; check battery terminals first
RecommendedAction: Bench-test starter; replace unit or solenoid
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Electrode wear past service interval; oil/carbon fouling; wrong heat range
PrecautionarySteps: Expect harder cold starts; avoid flooring the throttle
RecommendedAction: Replace plugs (and inspect coils); cheap fix with big drivability gains
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Blown fuse; corroded connector; chafed harness; rodent damage; failing relay
PrecautionarySteps: Check and replace the relevant fuse with the SAME rating only; never bypass a fuse
RecommendedAction: Trace the circuit if fuses keep blowing — repeated blowing signals a short
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Corroded core; cracked plastic end-tank; failed cap; stone damage
PrecautionarySteps: Top up coolant (correct type) only when engine is cool; watch the temp gauge constantly
RecommendedAction: Repair or replace radiator; do not rely on stop-leak products long-term
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Thermostat stuck open (runs cold) or closed (overheats); wax element failure
PrecautionarySteps: If running cold: expect poor heater and mileage. If overheating: stop driving immediately
RecommendedAction: Replace thermostat and gasket; inexpensive part
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Worn bearing/seal; corroded impeller; belt-driven pump nearing service life
PrecautionarySteps: Stop driving if temperature climbs; check for coolant trail under the engine
RecommendedAction: Replace pump (often done with timing belt); overheating risk is severe
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Age-hardened/cracked rubber; loose clamp; internal delamination
PrecautionarySteps: Never open the system hot; a swollen hose can burst — avoid driving
RecommendedAction: Replace the hose and clamp; inspect the other hoses at the same time
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Seized bearing; clutch failure; internal wear circulating debris
PrecautionarySteps: Switch the AC off to avoid belt damage; ventilation still works
RecommendedAction: Replace compressor; system must be flushed to remove debris
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: O-ring/seal leaks; condenser stone damage; corroded evaporator
PrecautionarySteps: Repeated top-ups without fixing the leak waste money and harm the environment
RecommendedAction: UV-dye leak test, repair the leak, then vacuum and recharge
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Worn motor brushes; failed blower resistor (single-speed symptom); connector burn

RecommendedAction: Replace blower resistor or motor
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Dust/pollen accumulation past replacement interval; leaf debris
PrecautionarySteps: Also causes windscreen fogging — reduces visibility in rain
RecommendedAction: Replace cabin filter (often DIY-able in minutes)
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Oil/gas seal failure; 60-80k km typical wear; rough-road usage
PrecautionarySteps: Braking distance increases — drive with extra margin; avoid high speed on uneven roads
RecommendedAction: Replace shocks in axle pairs; check bushes and mounts too
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Low PS fluid/leak; failed pump; EPS motor or torque-sensor fault; snapped belt

RecommendedAction: Check fluid/scan EPS immediately; loss of assist is a safety issue
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Bearing raceway wear; water/dirt ingress past seal; impact damage
PrecautionarySteps: Noise changing with steering input confirms it; avoid high speed — a seized bearing can lock a wheel
RecommendedAction: Replace the bearing/hub assembly soon
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Pothole/kerb impact; worn suspension components; incorrect toe/camber

RecommendedAction: Get a 4-wheel alignment; inspect suspension for bent parts first
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Boot torn letting grit in; age/pothole wear; lubrication loss
PrecautionarySteps: A failed ball joint can let the wheel fold under — treat clunks seriously; avoid rough roads
RecommendedAction: Inspect and replace worn joints urgently
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

ProbableCauses: Misalignment; incorrect pressures; worn shocks; unbalanced wheels
PrecautionarySteps: Check pressures monthly incl. spare; inspect tread depth across the width
RecommendedAction: Fix the root cause (alignment/suspension), rotate tyres, replace if below limit
ReferenceBasis: SAE J2012 OBD-II fault taxonomy; OEM service-manual categories; NHTSA/AAA public safety guidance

RecommendedAction: Have the tyre dismounted and properly patched from inside (avoid string plugs for highway use)
